stem: In preschool children, acute appendicitis may be more difficult to diagnose on abdominal examination. Which of these is LEAST common in this age group?
explanation: In younger children, appendicitis often presents atypically and perforation is relatively common because diagnosis is delayed. Faecolith-associated appendicitis is less characteristic in preschool children than in older children, and high-grade fever is not a typical early feature. The least common option here is high grade fever.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

rationale: Preserving the existing options and selecting the best single answer was possible. The question wording suggests an atypical feature in preschool appendicitis; among the provided options, high grade fever is least common.

optionExplanations.A: Less typical in preschool appendicitis; fever may be absent or only low grade early on.
optionExplanations.B: Perforation is relatively common in young children because diagnosis is often delayed.
optionExplanations.C: Faecoliths can occur, but this option is not the best answer here.
